comparison.normative_authority: Evaluation, requirements 9 and 15; alternative is not an adopted contract

audience: Readers who may be unfamiliar with both geospatial concepts and OpenUSD
purpose: Assess whether the proposal supplies sufficient, consistent data and observable rules for another implementer to derive meaningful results and tests
opening: USD describes a 3D model's shape and size. Geospatial information says where it belongs on Earth, so models, surveys and measurements can work together.
assessment: The full follow-up now starts from placement authoring: a readable heading/pitch/roll input, with explicit physical meaning and sample evaluation. The focused requirements baseline remains separate.
summary: All 105 prior case comparisons remain within their existing acceptance limits. New orientation and composition controls pass. Normal sampling remains unresolved; the preferred HPR model still needs group adoption.

cases.title: A geographic location for a 3D model
cases.question: Can a reader distinguish the model's shape from its location on Earth?
cases.rule: The scene records local geometry separately from its geographic origin and physical orientation. A coordinate reference system (CRS) defines how to interpret the origin's axes, units and height.
cases.expected: A reader has enough source information to place the model, without interpreting longitude or latitude as a distance or adding computed results to the source schema.
cases.observed: The source stores a single double3 heading/pitch/roll tuple in degrees. The rules define its true-north/ellipsoid-up meaning, rotation order and time-sample evaluation; computed quaternions stay transient.
cases.implication: The proposed representation follows the concrete authoring workflow. New checks show that reading, editing and composing these inputs produces the specified physical pose.
cases.boundary: This is the preferred local candidate, not group adoption. At +170 and -170 degrees the readers pass through 180 degrees; ordinary tuple interpolation would face 0 degrees.

cases.title: One physical place, different coordinates
cases.question: Does changing coordinate systems preserve physical placement?
cases.rule: CRS conversion expresses the same physical placement using different coordinates. The reader computes projection effects instead of recording them as additional source properties.
cases.expected: Longitude and latitude can become map east and north coordinates while the tower stays at the same physical place.
cases.observed: The illustration converts longitude, latitude and height into map coordinates. The physical site stays the same; map north and local scale can differ.
cases.implication: The proposed rules distinguish a new coordinate representation from a physical move. An image explains this distinction; numerical controls must test it.
cases.boundary: The location, height and orientation are illustrative. This image explains the proposed math and does not verify surveyed Paris placement.

cases.title: Ordinary model adjustments after placement
cases.question: In which coordinates do an author's scale, rotation and translation operate?
cases.rule: On an object with its own CRS binding, ordinary USD transforms (xformOps) adjust the resolved placement in a fixed project working frame. The requested output CRS does not reinterpret those adjustment values.
cases.expected: A project adjustment moves or resizes the placed model while its source geospatial inputs remain unchanged. The proposal separately specifies how child transforms retain model-local meaning.
cases.observed: The illustration applies scale 1.15, rotation 20 degrees, then moves 120 m east and 60 m south. A child-transform control separates two interpretations by 4.222 m.
cases.implication: Order changes the result. The control tests the agreed anchor/child distinction while detailed chart and instance conventions remain candidates.
cases.boundary: The image is informative. Feedback supports project adjustments versus model-local child offsets; detailed rules still need review.

image.alt: Illustrative Eiffel tower moves east and south after ordinary scale and rotation, with its previous position outlined in blue

cases.title: The same rules in two placement readers
cases.question: Can separate implementations derive the same coordinates from the proposed inputs and rules?
cases.rule: Consumers use the same declared coordinate meanings and resolution rules for a requested output. Agreement must be assessed with declared units and numerical evidence.
cases.expected: Python and C++ readers resolve the same partner points into matching output coordinates within the recorded tolerance.
cases.observed: France and Colorado points resolve through both readers. The maximum measured difference over the recorded coordinates is 3.39e-08 m.
cases.implication: The compared cases support reproducible interpretation of the proposed placement rules. They do not establish coverage of every rule or every input layout.
cases.boundary: Both readers use PROJ and share dataset decoding. Agreement is limited to tested domains and is not independent geodetic validation.

cases.title: Ordinary USD geometry for rendering
cases.question: Can a renderer use the result without implementing geospatial evaluation?
cases.rule: An explicit bake creates a derived copy containing resolved geometry and ordinary transforms. It retains the output coordinate context and applies each placement effect once.
cases.expected: A USD renderer reads the derived copy as ordinary geometry while the source scene keeps its authored geospatial inputs.
cases.observed: Native Hydra/Storm renders the ordinary USD bake. A double-precision origin keeps local points small; fresh readers recover the placement.
cases.implication: Unaware viewers receive resolved ordinary geometry. Fresh checks reject duplicate meshes and retain an unrelated applied schema.
cases.boundary: This is a recorded native render. General materials, primvars and continuous coverage remain unverified.

image.alt: Actual Hydra Storm render of the ordinary USD Eiffel bake on an illustrative ground plane

cases.title: Measurements stay paired with their locations
cases.question: Can the scene make a native measurement dataset usable without rewriting its values or guessing what its coordinates mean?
cases.rule: The scene identifies the asset, field and coordinate domain. The reader resolves sample locations while preserving their association with values, missing-data masks and observation times.
cases.expected: The same sample keeps the same measurement value and observation time whether its location is returned as longitude/latitude/height or Earth-centred Cartesian coordinates.
cases.observed: The synthetic global temperature case returns both coordinate forms for 154 samples and preserves the native values and two observation times.
cases.implication: The example exercises larger-scale analytical use, beyond model rendering. The proposal's association rule also identifies the later shared-decoder mistake as a failure.
cases.boundary: The values are synthetic. Named-dimension associations are independently tested; agreeing readers alone cannot verify shared decoding.

image.alt: Synthetic global temperature values shown at their longitude and latitude locations

cases.title: A construction site's own survey grid
cases.question: Can a project's local survey grid participate as a defined CRS?
cases.rule: Site calibration records how a local survey grid relates to a broader coordinate system. The source WKT, a standard text description, carries that relationship and its units.
cases.expected: The partner survey resolves into the calibrated site grid using US survey feet, separately from the scene's model units and up direction.
cases.observed: The original LandXML survey breaklines resolve and reach an ordinary USD bake rendered by Storm.
cases.implication: The case supports a site's calibrated CRS using partner survey lines. It does not establish independent survey accuracy.
cases.boundary: The image shows survey breaklines. It does not independently validate the survey or certify a continuous terrain surface.

image.alt: Actual Storm render of resolved Colorado survey breaklines in the calibrated site grid

requirements.title: A site's own grid is a CRS like any other.
The same answer for every consumer.

cases.title: Useful horizontal placement without invented height
cases.question: Can incomplete source metadata still support an honestly limited workflow?
cases.rule: A consumer does not invent missing coordinate meaning. An explicitly horizontal association can support horizontal resolution while leaving uninterpreted third components unchanged.
cases.expected: The horizontal copy resolves into the UTM 32 map system. The original GeoJSON remains unchanged, and no height reference is guessed.
cases.observed: The horizontal railway copy resolves 15,822 vertices across 2,386 parts. The plot uses display-only offsets.
cases.implication: This case exercises visible limits on interpretation, not a silent assumption that every three-number tuple is a valid geographic 3D position.
cases.boundary: The original third components remain uninterpreted. This demonstration supports horizontal placement only.

image.alt: Railway horizontal coordinates expressed in UTM 32 with display-only plotting offsets

cases.title: Animation evaluation order
cases.question: Does the proposal say how to resolve positions between authored moments?
cases.rule: Interpolate the authored source location first, then convert coordinates. Interpolating already-converted endpoints can produce a different path.
cases.expected: At the middle sample, both readers return the converted source-interpolated position. An ordinary bake states exactly which samples it preserves.
cases.observed: In the equatorial test, the source longitude spans 0 to 2 degrees. Interpolating converted endpoints misses the source-first midpoint by 971.421 m.
cases.implication: The distinguishing control makes the ordering rule testable. Preserving sample times alone cannot prove preservation of the original trajectory between samples.
cases.boundary: Position interpolation is shown here. HPR wrap, held samples, reference offsets and value clips pass separate controls.

status_rows: A focused requirements baseline is separate from the full candidate used for execution. Supported meaning and pending conventions are distinguished.
No additional undefined model rule was confirmed in reviewed paths. This is a scoped assessment, not an exhaustive completeness proof.
The selected cases work. 6 prior defects pass fresh counterexamples; 1 remains unresolved.
Coordinate epochs and scene-authored transformation resources remain on the roadmap. Initial choices must preserve a path to adding them.
input_rows: Shape and local distances, with declared model units and up direction. In USD: points, metersPerUnit and upAxis.
A CRS binding refers to WKT, the standard text description of the location's axes, units and height meaning.
crs:position locates the model origin. The illustrative example uses longitude 2.2945 degrees, latitude 48.8584 degrees and ellipsoidal height 80 m.
crs:orientation stores heading, pitch and roll in degrees: which way the model faces and tilts at its origin.
issue_rows: Remaining: normal sampling has no justified domain/error bound; projected difference about 1.24 degrees.
Corrected: an unbound library prototype receives its instancer placement in both readers.
Corrected: two source meshes yield exactly two baked meshes; extras are rejected.
Corrected: all six measurements retain the coordinates declared by dimension names.
Corrected: the bake retains MotionAPI and its velocity-scale value.
Corrected: reports include component errors, magnitudes and angular errors.
Corrected: both readers reject an invalid child placement field.
placement_choice_rows: Preferred HPR tuple in degrees, with explicit pose interpolation. Authored inputs only; adoption pending.

Specify equivalence criteria and the comparison domain, accounting for relevant axes, units and metadata.
Declare the composed scene's need for geospatial interpretation, including unloaded content. Writers and assemblers maintain the declaration.
Record a Cartesian CRS and ordinary double-precision origin. Preserve precision and space/time coverage.
evidence_rows: 213,243 coordinate results per reader. Maximum measured difference 3.39e-08 m. They share PROJ and native dataset decoding.
Reuses Python placement. Recorded readback covers 177,872 geometry vertices and 48 edit, failure and recovery checks, across 39 jobs.
Two selected ordinary USD bakes reach native rendering. This consumer path uses the C++ placement results.
88 regressions and 65 distinguishing controls passed. Fresh independent diagnostics verify six repairs and retain the unresolved normal case.
Original inputs and all frozen execution files remained unchanged during this run. The immutable receipt identifies the exact executed content.
11 selected exports were checked. The fresh nested-geometry counterexample verifies the complete inventory, including unexpected extras.
provenance_disposition: Fresh October 8 execution of the local stacked follow-up, with clause-traced adapter repairs and repeated independent diagnostics. No changes have been published.

run_comparison.explanation: This run tests the full model/runtime follow-up after choosing the authoring representation. The focused terms/requirements branch is unchanged.
rows: All 31 requirement IDs remain. The requirements-only branch is unchanged; this run uses the full local follow-up.
A single authored heading/pitch/roll tuple lets authors read and correct physical placement directly. It is the preferred candidate, not group consensus.
Select composed HPR samples, convert each to a pose, then interpolate. Reference time offsets, value clips and shortest-path wrap have fresh controls.
Dimension-name ordering, invalid-placement failures and required precision-preserving ordinary USD bakes are explicit.
All 105 prior comparisons pass existing acceptance limits; 102 are exactly equal. Four orientation jobs extend reader and consumer coverage.
Six counterexamples pass after repair; normal sampling still lacks justified approximation evidence.
Input-only physical meaning and anchor/descendant distinction have supportive feedback. Preferred HPR storage and detailed carrier/chart conventions await adoption.
